This text is from the Sumerian creation myth, often associated with the "Enki and Ninmah" or related cosmogonic compositions. Here is a translation:

1. In those days, in those days when heaven and earth had been fashioned,
2. In those nights, in those nights when heaven and earth had been fashioned,
3. In those years, in those years when the fates had been decreed,
4. When the Anunnaki had been born,
5. When the goddess Ama-dinana had been taken for lordship,
6. When the goddess Ama-dinana had been distributed throughout heaven and earth,
7. When the goddess Ama-dinana had [...] multiplied and given birth,
8. When the gods' food rations had been bound to their dwellings,
9. The senior gods were overseeing the work, (while) the lesser gods were bearing the toil,
10. The gods were digging the watercourses, they were piling up the silt of them in Ḫarali,
11. The gods who were grinding the clay — they were complaining about their life,
12. At that time, the one of broad wisdom, the creator of all the great gods,
13. Enki, in the deep Engur, the subterranean water — a place whose interior no other god could gaze upon —
14. was lying on his bed, and would not rise from his sleep.
15. The gods were weeping with tears, they were saying: "There is lamentation!"
16. He who was lying in sleep — from his bed he would not arise.
17. Namma, the mother, the ancestress who gave birth to all the great gods,
18. brought the tears of the gods to her son,
19. "[...] you have been lying down, you have been sleeping,
20. [...] you do not rise!
21. The creatures fashioned by your hand — their ... are bowed down (with toil)."

This passage describes the primordial era before the creation of humankind, when the gods themselves had to perform labor. The senior gods imposed work on the lesser gods, who toiled digging canals and moving earth. They complained bitterly while Enki slept in the underground waters. Finally, the mother-goddess Namma brought the gods' lament to Enki, urging him to wake and devise a solution — which would ultimately lead to the creation of humans to bear the gods' burden.
